subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should same-session webhook deliveries be rejected with 409, queued/serialized, or left parallel by default, and should any non-parallel behavior be opt-in per hook or mapping?
rationale: This changes an external Gateway HTTP webhook contract and retry semantics for existing integrations, so automation should not choose the permanent overlap policy.

options.title: Opt-in overlap policy
options.body: Add an explicit hook or mapping policy such as `skip`, `queue`, or `parallel` while preserving today's default behavior for existing callers.

options.title: Unconditional 409 guard
options.body: Implement the reporter's exact behavior for every same-session active hook delivery and accept the compatibility break for callers that currently expect `200`/`runId`.

options.title: Fold into queued webhooks
options.body: Defer this specific guard until the queued-webhook design chooses durable backlog, parallelism, and caller response semantics together.

recommendation.title: Opt-in overlap policy
recommendation.body: Add an explicit hook or mapping policy such as `skip`, `queue`, or `parallel` while preserving today's default behavior for existing callers.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-cutting Gateway hook/session compatibility decision, and steipete has adjacent hook-session and isolated-run history plus routing signal in the issue timeline.
